subject: Meteorology
title: Thunder
description: A fast breakdown of Thunder for builders.

hook.text: Thunder is the shockwave from lightning—rapid heating of air creates an explosive expansion that we hear as sound.

buildup.text: The superheated air expands so fast it creates a sonic boom—a pressure wave radiating outward from the channel.

discovery.text: Thunder rumbles because sound arrives at different times from different parts of the lightning channel.

twist.text: You can estimate storm distance: count seconds between flash and thunder, divide by three—that's kilometers away.

climax.text: Thunder is rarely heard beyond 25 km—sound bends upward in warm air near the surface and dissipates.

punchline.text: If you hear thunder, lightning is close enough to strike you.

quiz.question: Why does thunder rumble?
options: Sound arriving from different parts of the channel at different times
